OncallBot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT OPENED - Sev2 - GPU pool exhaustion, autoscaler failing to launch new nodes (1862345600)
SRE Pager: Paging Alex (oncall) and Maria (sre) - high queue growth observed across inference-gpu pools.
Alex: I'm on it, looking at the dashboard. queues spiking across eu-west-1 and us-central.
Maria: I see continuous enqueue rate ~250 r/s and worker count pegged at 0 new nodes. Autoscaler showing repeated errors.
Alex: Any obvious error from the autoscaler logs?
Jordan: grabbing logs now, looks like cloud API 429s when creating instances. sending tail:
Jordan: ```
2026-03-14T18:00:12Z autoscaler: instance create failed: quotaExceeded -> 429 Too Many Requests
2026-03-14T18:00:13Z autoscaler: retry attempt 3/5 backoff=2s
2026-03-14T18:00:15Z autoscaler: instance create failed: provider API rate limit
```
Lee: Confirmed - our provider returned rate-limits on compute API, autoscaler retries but backoff too short and we hit the per-project burst cap.
Alex: Impact? Which customers are affected? Priya, can you pull top active tenants?
Priya: Sending list, top 5 affected tenants are proprietary-retailer, docs-search, chat-bot-team. Some customers reporting 503s and high latency. We're triaging support tickets.
Samir: Noted customer impact. Are Hosted API customers on dedicated capacity affected?
Maria: Only those routed to the exhausted GPU pools. We have some dedicated pools with spare capacity, but routing/policy didn't failover because model variants mismatch.
Alex: Short-term mitigation plan: 1) divert new requests to a fallback CPU/quantized pool for non-critical models; 2) manually spin emergency nodes in a different project/region that still has quota; 3) increase autoscaler backoff and add jitter to reduce thundering.
Jordan: Working on route change. I can update the smart routing policy to prefer fallback pools for specified models. Pushing change now.
Jordan: ```PATCH routing-policy: prefer=fallback-quantized when latency_slo>200ms OR pool_util>90%```
Alex: Lee, can you attempt manual instance create in us-west-2 with a different service account?
Lee: Trying `gcloud compute instances create rwi-emergency-1 --zone=us-west2-a --machine-type=a2-highgpu-1 --project=redwood-emergency` now
Lee: Got provisioning OK in the emergency project. Instances up and kube nodes joined cluster -> pods scheduling.
Maria: Good. I'm adjusting autoscaler config: bump backoff base to 8s, max retries to 8, add exponential jitter. Patching now.
Maria: ```yaml
scalePolicy:
  retryBackoffBaseSeconds: 8
  retryBackoffMaxSeconds: 120
  jitter: true
```
SRE Pager: Noted change. Will monitor.
Jordan: Routing change deployed, about 30% of new requests now landing on fallback-quantized pool. Queue growth flattening.
Alex: Monitoring token-level latency/cost. Any errors from model compatibility?
Jordan: A couple of generation mismatches for high-end models; we return compatibility fallback and a warning header. Customers affected: chat-bot-team (minor quality degradation).
Priya: Support is updating customers: degraded latency or quality for short window, but we switched them to fallback to avoid full outages. Many customers appreciated proactive message.
Samir: Good customer message. Let's confirm root cause and followups after stabilizing.
SRE Pager: Current metrics -> queue length down 70% over 10m, worker utilization steady, no further 429s from emergency project.
Alex: Great. Continuing to monitor for 30m. After that we'll convene postmortem.
-- 22 minutes later --
Alex: System stable for 25m. Autoscaler backoff + emergency nodes kept queues below threshold.
Maria: Start of incident summary for postmortem:
Maria: "Cause: Provider API rate limiting on primary project (project-level burst quota) caused autoscaler create requests to fail. Autoscaler retried with insufficient backoff -> thundering retry pattern. Routing policy didn't fallback because of strict model compatibility checks. Result: queue growth and degraded customer latency; partial mitigation via manual emergency nodes and routing to quantized fallback pool."
Jordan: Adding logs and timeline to the incident doc.
Alex: Action items: 
- Lee: Create runbook step to verify provider project-level API quotas and add guardrail to autoscaler to detect persistent 429s -> trigger emergency fallback (DUTY: Lee).
- Maria: Improve autoscaler retry strategy and add hysteresis to avoid repeated simultaneous retries (DUTY: Maria).
- Jordan: Enhance routing policy to allow compatibility-based fallbacks automatically for subset of models and flag quality degradation in response headers (DUTY: Jordan).
- Priya/Samir: Draft customer communication template for capacity-exhaustion events and include in on-call playbook (DUTY: Priya; review Samir).
- Alex: Run quarterly chaos test to simulate provider API rate limits and verify emergency flows (DUTY: Alex).
Alex: Assigning owners in our tracking board now. Will schedule postmortem doc and link to this thread.
Priya: I already sent the interim customer note to affected accounts. No escalations so far.
Maria: Follow-up note - autoscaler metrics to add: provider_429_count, retry_backoff_stats, pending_create_queue_length.
Lee: I'll add alerting: if provider_429_count > 10/min for 5m -> pagers and auto-trigger routing fallback.
SRE Pager: Recording incident close when last check passes for 1h.
Alex: Thank you all. Closing channel for active mitigation, will reopen for postmortem. :white_check_mark:
Priya: Thanks team.
Samir: Appreciate the quick coordination.
OncallBot: INCIDENT CLOSED (awaiting postmortem) - Incident duration ~48m
